# ACC010 `private-array-in-contained-kernel`

<Badge type="info" text="info" /> <Badge type="info" text="opt-in" />

A compute region of a contained (internal) procedure has a private array.

## Why

nvfortran has been observed to mis-privatise arrays listed in `private` inside OpenACC kernels of
*contained* procedures: runtime-sized private arrays get garbage that depends on the gang count,
and even fixed-size ones can bleed between threads. Advisory: prefer scalar accumulation, or move
the kernel to a module procedure, and verify against a CPU run.

## Reported

```fortran
contains
  subroutine fill()
    real :: buf(5)
    !$acc parallel loop private(buf)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
! module procedure, or scalar temporaries instead of buf(5)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[ACC010] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = ACC010` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).
